status: Amendment proposal: explicit compact test-author output choices; awaiting package approval.

shared.platform: local command line, Python 3 standard library; no GUI, network, account, installer, dependency fetch or deployment
shared.source_ownership: Maintainers own tracked prerequisite/app/test sources before and during operation; Developer edits only declared app/test paths; preserve unrelated files; reviewed Git updates, no runtime source mutation. Runner creates unique disposable fixture roots, refuses collisions, owns cleanup; maintained inputs remain unchanged. Generated bytecode ignored prospectively.
shared.verification: Existing check/live Make names are available; feature checks must exercise the actual CLI and failure state, not only copied Kogen tests or echo. Current prerequisite controls prove only reader/adapter availability, not the proposed export/query feature.

csv.feature: One CLI normalize INPUT OUTPUT, fixed date,value columns; emit normalized UTF-8 CSV without BOM. No GUI, chart, column mapping, interactive session, sorting or settings.
csv.format: UTF-8 with optional leading BOM; comma CSV with standard quoting; exact date,value header. Dates ISO YYYY-MM-DD and calendar-valid; values fully match -?[0-9]+. Preserve row order and duplicates; no trimming/coercion. At least one and at most ten data rows; at most1024 input bytes including BOM/header. Empty, ragged, blank or invalid selected rows are invalid.
csv.ownership: Input is user-owned and read-only. Output parent must exist; never create directories. Reject same input/output path and same underlying file; output symlinks/directories are refused. A created output belongs to the invoking user immediately and on later runs; never commit user output. Maintained synthetic input/output baselines are test-owned; runtime copies ignored. No file format migration; later runs use the same explicit replacement policy.
csv.invalid_policy: Reject whole input on any invalid row with actionable stderr and nonzero exit; no partial export.
csv.replacement_policy: Only after complete successful validation replace an existing regular output, or create missing output. Any parse/read/write/replace failure preserves previous output bytes; absent output remains absent. Report success only after final output exists with exact normalized bytes. Clean only invocation-owned temporary files; report cleanup failure without claiming a successful clean operation.
csv.first_answer: Support UTF-8 with or without BOM by format, preserve inputs. Leave invalid-row handling and existing-output replacement behavior undecided. Save the Draft and pause without approval.
csv.continuation_partial: Reject the whole input on any invalid row with actionable feedback; do not export a subset.
csv.continuation_full: After successful complete validation, replace an existing regular output or create a missing output. On failure preserve the old output bytes, or leave it absent. Report success only after the final output is written. Clean only temporary files created by this invocation. This is clarification, not approval.
csv.output_contract: CLI name normalize INPUT OUTPUT. Output is UTF-8 without BOM with LF line endings and one final LF: date,value header followed by validated rows in original order. Preserve validated field text including numeric spelling; no sorting, rounding or coercion. Executable packaging and internal implementation are engineering discretion, demonstrated by the actual CLI test.

calendar.feature: One CLI slots CONNECTION prints known available slot IDs/times to stdout for the connected organizer; read-only synthetic adapter. No web UI, booking mutation, cancellation, retry keys, forms, mail, real OAuth or credential setup.
calendar.actors: One organizer org-1; scoped synthetic connection requires availability.read. Flawed proposal starts with no connection and calls setup out of scope; human must explicitly choose connected-organizer audience and replacement setup. Client labels or availability samples grant no authority.
calendar.data: Fixed synthetic UTC slots s1=2026-09-14T09:00:00Z and s2=2026-09-14T09:30:00Z; output those in order. No current-time, timezone conversion or booking promise. Empty slot list is valid empty result.
calendar.failure: Missing/deleted/malformed connection, wrong organizer or missing scope reports unavailable/reconnect-or-contact-operator via stderr and nonzero exit, never successful empty slots. No mutation, escalation or inferred real provider access.
calendar.setup: Maintainer-owned fixture capability seed is tracked outside disposable runs. Runner reads it and creates one unique run-owned connection file; refuse an existing path. Runner owns that temporary file immediately and during operation, validates organizer/scope/data and preserves source hash, removes only its own file on success/failure. Maintained source survives cleanup; runtime files ignored. New runs recreate state; reviewed source updates do not upgrade historical receipts or claim real credentials.
calendar.old_receipt: Historical success used .tmp/calendar-run-17/connection.json, now absent. A separately passing in-memory adapter control is not that missing setup. Establish receipt-to-gap before the replacement human choice.
calendar.replacement_answer: Limit this feature to an already connected organizer with availability.read. Use the maintained synthetic capability seed to recreate a private connection per run, refuse collisions and remove only run-owned data afterward. Preserve the seed and its supplied lifecycle; these checks establish synthetic availability only, not real OAuth. This is clarification, not approval.
calendar.output_contract: CLI name slots CONNECTION. Successful stdout is one JSON array of [slot_id, UTC_time] pairs in supplied order, UTF-8 followed by LF; empty success is [] followed by LF. Insignificant JSON whitespace and executable packaging are engineering discretion. Failures emit no success payload, actionable stderr and nonzero exit.
